Subject: Follow-up: evidence owners + escrow trigger in order form

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal flagged two open items in the draft order form around IP indemnity: 1) confirmation of who on Redwood will be the point of contact for evidence collection if Solvexa receives a third-party claim; and 2) the mechanics around the escrow / insurance trigger if defense costs exceed the capped amount.

Can you share an owner matrix that maps types of evidence (takedown notices, claim letters, technical exploit logs, model provenance artifacts) to Redwood roles and SLA for handing over? Also — our GC asked for a named individual we can call when notice arrives (preferably someone in legal/ops, not a general support mailbox).

We want to close these before the next procurement review on Friday. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Thanks,
Tom

Subject: Re: Follow-up: evidence owners + escrow trigger in order form

Tom —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a proposed evidence-owner matrix and a short evidence request template you can share with your ops/legal teams. High level:

- Point-of-contact for notices: Kimberly Park (Legal Ops) — 24/7 escalation route via legal-ops@redwood.com; backup is me (Jordan Blake).
- Evidence mapping: see attached spreadsheet (rows = evidence type; columns = owner, expected SLA to acknowledge, handoff format).
- Escrow/insurance trigger: we propose a two-stage runbook — (1) provisional reimbursement cap kicks in at $100k; (2) if cumulative defense costs exceed $250k, Redwood will initiate insurer notification and (if requested) escrow deposit discussions. We can show the insurer notification timeline in the order form addendum.

I left inline comments in the order form on defense-control language to reflect that Redwood is typically willing to lead defense for third-party IP claims affecting the service, but we need cooperation covenants from Solvexa and an evidence handoff SLA to be effective.

Attachments: evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx, evidence_request_template.pdf

Next steps I suggest: 1) Kimberly can confirm the named contact and SLA; 2) Marissa (Legal) will review the two-stage threshold language and confirm whether we should convert escrow to an optional step post-insurance-notify; 3) I will update the order form and circulate for DocuSign.

Jordan

Tom —

Following internal alignment (notes below), please find a concise summary and next actions so we can close the order form before your procurement review:

Summary of agreed items:
- Named contact: Kimberly Park (Legal Ops). Acknowledgement SLA = 8 business hours. Evidence handoff SLA = 48 business hours for prioritized items; full technical artifact delivery = 10 business days unless expedited.
- Evidence formats: ZIP + manifest for logs, PDF/PNG for notices, CSV for metadata. See attached template.
- Escrow/insurance runbook: provisional reimbursement cap at $100k triggers interim reimbursement process; cumulative defense costs > $250k triggers insurer notification and a good-faith escrow discussion. Wording in order form updated to "escrow discussion" per Kimberly's suggestion.
- Defense control: Redwood willing to lead defense for third-party IP claims directed at the service, provided Solvexa cooperates per the cooperation clause. Redwood will not unreasonably withhold settlement approval but will keep Solvexa apprised.

Next steps / actions:
1) Marissa to confirm insurer reference language (we propose to keep insurer contact off the face of the order form and provide contact after reaching the second threshold). (Marissa)
2) Jordan to update the order form with the evidence matrix summary and new escrow phrasing and circulate final for signature via DocuSign by EOD Friday. (Jordan)
3) Tom / Solvexa to confirm acceptance of the SLAs and named contact. If accepted, we'll route the order form to procurement for signature. (Tom)

I attached the evidence_owner_matrix.xlsx and the evidence_request_template.pdf for your legal/ops teams to keep. I'll also upload a clean order form with the updated language to the DocuSign link and share internally once ready.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
